arguments.title: COM458 NYC shot direction
arguments.message:
I'm the video editor for ComfortWear. I need you to DIRECT this ad: tell me exactly which scene goes on screen for every line of the VO, and what text goes where. I will source and cut the footage.

## The ad: COM458 (Travel/NYC iteration of our winner COM376, "Worst shoes for Disney")
Execution style: Mash-Up. Our ads perform best when the B-roll is ORGANIC UGC of the exact place/angle being talked about — for NYC that means real NYC UGC phone footage (subway stairs, Manhattan sidewalks, bagel lines, Central Park benches, Brooklyn Bridge, Broadway, slush/icy curbs, Uber at night...), sourced from TikTok/YouTube. Product scenes come from our own ComfortWear Ortho Stretch footage (knit slip-on sneaker, wide toe box, stretch knit, arch insole, orange/black slip-resistant outsole). We can also generate AI shots (e.g. an AI podiatrist in a lab coat, 3D foot-in-shoe animations with red pressure glow) when UGC can't show it.

## Hooks (3 variants, shared body)
Hook 1 VO: Hokas and On Clouds are the worst shoes you can pack for New York City. I know that'll upset people, but it is not the brand. It is the design. | Super: HOKAS & ON CLOUDS ARE THE WORST SHOES FOR NYC
Hook 2 VO: If you just spent nearly two hundred dollars on Hokas or On Clouds specifically for your New York trip, do not put them in your suitcase. Those plush gym shoes are built for forty minutes on a treadmill, not 20,000 steps on unforgiving city concrete. | Super: YOU'LL REGRET PACKING HOKAS OR ON CLOUD FOR NYC
Hook 3 VO: Watch what happens to anyone wearing Hokas or On Clouds around two in the afternoon in New York. They'll be either icing their heels in the hotel or paying 40 dollars for a cab because their feet completely tapped out before dinner. | Super: WHY NYC TOURISTS TAP OUT BY 2 PM

## Body (VO | Super)
P1: These shoes are built to move a runner forward for forty minutes, not for someone exploring New York City. When you are visiting Manhattan, you are not just walking. You are pounding solid concrete, climbing three flights of subway stairs, navigating cracked pavement, standing in lines for hours, and doing it all for eight, nine, sometimes ten hours straight. Three things people overlook until they are already in the city. | BUILT FOR 40-MIN RUNS / NOT 20,000 STEPS ON NYC CONCRETE
P2: Number one, that soft foam feeling and those bouncy pods do not tell you the whole story. With Hokas, that thick soft foam is made to spring a runner forward on a jog. But New York means walking six blocks, standing in line for a bagel, waiting on a concrete subway platform, and standing through a museum tour because the line does not get shorter when your feet start aching from the foam packing flat. And with On Clouds, those hollow open pods compress down under constant concrete standing, leaving your arch with zero support right when you need it most. | 1. HOKA FOAM PACKS FLAT / ON CLOUD PODS FLATTEN
P3: Number two, Hokas and On Clouds were not built for city streets and winter hazards. In New York, you are walking across cracked pavement, stepping off icy curbs, and hurrying down steep subway stairs for hours. You want to feel steady with every step. With Hokas, that massive, tall stack height shifts your balance, making you wobble over frozen slush and putting extra strain directly on your knees and ankles. Plus, all that thick foam makes them heavy to lift over twenty thousand steps. And with On Clouds, those smooth pod outsoles turn into literal ice skates the second winter slush, snow, or freezing rain hits polished station tile and metal subway grates. That is where a slip-resistant outsole matters. You want a shoe with real grip, not an unstable sole or slippery pods on freezing streets. | 2. HOKA MAKES YOU WOBBLE / ON CLOUDS ARE SLICK ON SNOW & ICE
P4: Number three, the toe box is narrow, and it does not stretch. On Clouds are notoriously narrow to lock a runner tight, and Hokas taper sharply at the toes. If they squeeze your toes together before you have even left the hotel, that is not a promising start. After hours of walking eight to ten miles across the city, your feet naturally swell. A tight fit becomes the only thing you can think about. Your toes feel trapped, rubbing blisters with every single block. You are loosening your laces on a bench in Central Park, and you have still got dinner and a Broadway show to go. | 3. ON CLOUDS TOO NARROW / HOKAS TAPER
P5: That is why Comfortwear built the opposite of a running shoe, made for people whose feet have to get through real life: nurses, healthcare workers, and travelers who want to actually enjoy the trip they have been saving for. A roomy toe box lets your toes spread out instead of getting squeezed together. A flexible stretch knit upper gives your feet room as they swell throughout the day. Comfortable cushioning and built-in arch support work together underfoot so the support never packs flat, paired with a slip-resistant outsole for added traction on wet crosswalks, subway stairs, and metal grates. | BUILT FOR REAL LIFE / ROOMY TOE BOX + EXPANDING KNIT / ARCH SUPPORT NEVER PACKS FLAT
P6: Because you do not want to be the person cutting the day short, sitting on a bench in Soho watching everyone else explore, or tapping out and paying fifty dollars for an Uber back to the hotel. You want to be walking the Brooklyn Bridge, exploring every neighborhood, and there when the curtain goes up at the theater. | DO NOT MISS OUT / KEEP UP ALL DAY / ZERO FOOT PAIN
P7: Right now during their Holiday Sale, Comfortwear is up to forty percent off with free shipping, putting them under sixty dollars, and you get thirty days to try them. Put them through your long walking days before your trip. If they are not right for you, send them back. Tap below and grab your pair before you pack for New York. | HOLIDAY SALE / UP TO 40% OFF / UNDER $60 + FREE SHIPPING / 30-DAY WEAR-TEST GUARANTEE

## How the winner COM376 is edited (match this exactly)
- 134 s, 98 cuts, median shot 1.3 s. Cut on almost every caption phrase; every noun gets its literal shot ("Epcot" = Epcot UGC, "cobblestone streets" = POV feet on cobblestone, "standing in line for hours" = crowded queue).
- Hook (0-3 s): close-up of hands on a real worn Hoka, then POV UGC walking in the park. Stacked headline box (white rounded box, line 1 RED caps "HOKAS AND BROOKS", lines 2-3 black caps "ARE THE WORST SHOES YOU CAN WEAR FOR DISNEY"), mid-frame. No captions under it.
- 3-6.5 s: AI podiatrist in lab coat, clinic, says "I know that'll upset people / It's not the brand, it's the design" with a lower-third "Dr. Moore, DPM" + blue "PODIATRIST PHYSICIAN".
- Running captions everywhere else: black bold sans on white rounded boxes, 2-5 words, 1-2 lines, around 65-70% height.
- Section headlines as numbered listicle: "#1 - SOFT FOAM BUILT FOR RUNNING", "#2 - NON-SLIP GRIP SOLE", "#3 - WIDE TOE-BOX" — white bold caps, black outline, top third, held over the 3-4 shots that open each section, then dropped.
- Problem sections: competitor shoe on feet / on runners, then UGC of the location, then a 3D foot-in-shoe animation with red pressure/squeeze glow on "aching" / "toes trapped".
- Solution: product demos matched word-for-word (toe box spread by hands, knit stretch, insole, slip-resistant sole flipped, standing on a balance pad).
- Payoff: happy UGC moments at the destination (rides, photo, fireworks).
- Offer: 3D "40% OFF" sticker pops over blurred product, red "FREE SHIPPING" ribbon slaps on, gold "30 DAYS MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE" badge, then walking shots, then the ComfortWear end card ("TAKE ADVANTAGE OF DISCOUNTS / 40% OFF SITEWIDE").

## What I need from you
Direct COM458 shot-by-shot for Hook 1, Hook 2, Hook 3 and the full body, in the same style. For EVERY shot give:
1. the VO words it covers (exact phrase, in order, no gaps),
2. the visual (specific, filmable/findable: e.g. "POV phone UGC climbing grimy subway stairs at Times Sq station, crowd ahead"),
3. source: NYC_UGC / COMPETITOR_UGC (Hoka or On Cloud on feet) / PRODUCT (our footage) / AI (give the generation prompt) / ANIMATION,
4. a TikTok search query I should use to find it (for UGC rows),
5. on-screen text: say whether this shot carries the HOOK HEADLINE, a SECTION HEADLINE (give exact words), an OFFER GRAPHIC, or just the running caption.
Also tell me which brief "Super" lines should become on-screen headlines and which are better left to captions, and where you'd put the AI doctor (if at all) for each hook. Keep all competitor claims framed as opinion. Output as a numbered shot list per section, then a short list of the top 15 NYC UGC search queries.
